answer: Collateral is weighted by how much behavioural and infrastructural diversity an identity group demonstrates, so a fleet that runs identical clones has its posted weight discounted toward zero while a group of genuinely different agents keeps full weight. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Read it as an ocean weighed by marble against every prism nearby: identical prism groups cancel the marble and strip the ocean of value, while a prism with its own history keeps both.
